text.en: Nandini and Chirag go to see their Nani Maa. Nandini has 7 balushahi in her box and Chirag has 5 in his. They carry sweets, magazines, story books and stamps for Nani Maa. Along the way they add and take away, count stamps and radishes, jump on number lines and solve magic puzzles.

Nandini has 7 balushahi and Chirag has 5, so together they have 7 + 5 = 12 balushahi. If Nandini eats 5 of her 7 balushahi, we take away to find what is left: 7 - 5 = 2. Adding means joining groups, and taking away means finding what is left or what is missing. A tens frame helps us see small sums: to find 6 + 8, fill 8 boxes and then 6 more, and notice a full ten and 4 extra, so the answer is 14.
Nandini and Chirag have 15 stamps and get 7 more. We can find 15 + 7 by taking one jump of 7 or by breaking the jump into easier parts. One way is 15 + 5 = 20 and then 20 + 2 = 22. Another way is to jump 10 to 25 and come back 3 steps, because 15 + 10 - 3 = 22. Different jumps give the same answer, so we can choose the path that feels easiest to us. The number line can start at any number, and the jumps may be drawn unequal. What matters is that we write each jump we take. To subtract on the line we jump backward. To find 52 - 37, we can go back 37 or count up from 37 to 52 and see that the jumps add up to 15.
Nani Maa has 25 red radishes and 36 white radishes. We add 25 + 36 by making bundles of ten and loose sticks. Two bundles and 5 sticks join three bundles and 6 sticks. That is 5 bundles and 11 sticks, and 11 sticks make another bundle with 1 left, so the total is 61 radishes. Before we calculate we estimate. 25 is close to 30 and 36 is close to 40, so the answer should be near 70, and 61 is a sensible answer. A box diagram shows the whole as one long box and the parts inside it. If a box holds 100 vegetables and 65 are tomatoes, the rest are carrots, so 100 - 65 = 35 carrots.
Nandini picked 85 apples and Chirag picked 67. Since 85 + 20 is 105, we already know the total is more than 100. Exactly, 85 + 67 = 152. To find who picked more, we compare the two boxes: 85 - 67 = 18, so Nandini picked 18 apples more. Words like more, total and sum point to addition. Words like less, take away, difference and reduce point to subtraction. The number grid from 1 to 100 helps us move: adding 10 moves one row up, and adding 1 moves one step to the right.
In a magic square of the numbers 1 to 9, every row, every column and both diagonals add up to the same number, 15. In the square 2 7 6, 9 5 1, 4 3 8 the first row is 2 + 7 + 6 = 15 and the middle column is 7 + 5 + 3 = 15. Puzzles with row and column totals teach us to use what we know to find what is missing.
Nani Maa has a magic trick for Nandini and Chirag. They hide some marbles under a handkerchief, and Nani Maa tells how many are hidden. The secret is knowing which number makes a total. If there are 15 seeds in all and 12 are on the table, then 3 are hidden, because 12 and 3 make 15. Practise like this. Say a number between 1 and 9, and your friend says the number that makes 9. If you say 4, your friend says 5. Then try with 10 and with 20. Knowing pairs that make 10 helps a lot. 3 and 7 make 10, 6 and 4 make 10, and 8 and 2 make 10.
A tens frame has ten boxes, five in each row. It helps us add quickly because we can see a full ten. To find 6 + 8, put 8 dots in the frame. Two boxes are empty, so we move 2 dots from the 6. Now the frame is full, that is 10, and 4 dots are left. So 6 + 8 = 14. Use the frame for 5 + 10 and you get 15. For taking away, 9 - 6 = 3, and 18 - 9 = 9. Chirag got 9 story books for Nani Maa and Nandini got 7 puzzle books. Together that is 9 + 7 = 16 books.
Here is a game. Make four sets of cards with numbers from 1 to 10 and put them face down. Take turns to open one card at a time. If any three open cards make an addition or subtraction fact, you keep all three. For example, 2, 4 and 6 work because 2 + 4 = 6. When all cards are opened, the player with the most cards wins.
The children had 22 stamps. Nani Maa's brother gave them 30 more. We add 22 + 30 = 52 stamps now. Of the 52 stamps, 37 have faces of famous people. The rest have pictures of monuments. To find them, we jump back from 52: 52 - 37 = 15 monuments stamps. Next time they will have 75 stamps. They have 52 now, so they need 75 - 52 = 23 more. On the number line, jump from 52 to 60 is 8, then from 60 to 75 is 15. 8 + 15 = 23. Different jumps give the same answer. Choose the jump you like best.
The number grid has numbers from 1 to 100. Moving one box to the right adds 1, and moving one row up adds 10. In the grid game, you roll two dice to make a two-digit number and move your counter by that much. Nandini is at 23 and gets 11. She can move up one row to 33, then one step right to 34. If you cannot go forward, you may move backward. The first player to reach a number between 91 and 100 wins.

problem.en: Nandini and Chirag have 15 stamps and get 7 more. How many stamps do they have now?

text.en: We join the stamps, so we add: 15 + 7.
Jump 5 to reach 20 and then 2 more to reach 22.

why.en: Breaking 7 into 5 and 2 makes the jump easy.

text.en: They have 22 stamps now.

problem.en: Nani Maa has 25 red radishes and 36 white radishes. How many radishes does she have?

text.en: Estimate first: 25 is near 30 and 36 is near 40, so about 70.

why.en: An estimate tells us what size of answer to expect.

text.en: Add the tens: 20 + 30 = 50. Add the ones: 5 + 6 = 11.

why.en: Splitting each number into tens and ones.

text.en: 50 + 11 = 61 radishes.

why.en: 61 is close to our estimate of 70.

problem.en: A box has 100 vegetables. 65 are tomatoes. How many are carrots?

text.en: The whole is 100 and one part is 65, so we need the other part.

why.en: Draw a box diagram to see the parts.

text.en: Count up from 65 to 100: 5 more makes 70 and 30 more makes 100, so 35.
There are 35 carrots.

problem.en: Nandini and Chirag have 52 stamps. They want 75 stamps in all. How many more do they need?

text.en: Start at 52 on the number line. Jump 8 to reach 60.
From 60 jump 15 to reach 75.
Add the jumps: 8 + 15 = 23. They need 23 more stamps.

problem.en: Use a tens frame to find 7 + 6.

text.en: Put 7 dots in the frame. Three boxes are empty.

why.en: We want to fill the frame to make 10.

text.en: Move 3 dots from the 6 into the frame. Now it is full, that is 10, and 3 dots are left.

why.en: We add the full ten and the leftover.

prompt.en: Explain two different ways to find 48 + 25 on a number line.

requiredIdeas.en: Break one number into tens and ones
Use a friendly jump such as 25 = 20 + 5

commonMisconceptions.en: The jumps have to be equal in length
There is only one correct way to jump

points.en: We add to join groups and subtract to find what is left, how many more or the difference.
A number line lets us jump forward to add and backward to subtract, in any friendly steps.
Estimating first tells us whether an answer is sensible.
A box diagram shows the whole and its parts, which helps us choose the operation.
A magic square has all rows, columns and diagonals with the same sum.
Number pairs that make 9, 10 and 20 help us find a hidden number.
A tens frame helps us make a ten: 6 + 8 = 10 + 4 = 14.
To find how many more are needed, take away the smaller number from the bigger one: 75 - 52 = 23.
The number grid helps us add: right is +1 and up is +10.
